sentences.text:
The instant Appeal has been listed for passing appropriate order on the instant Interlocutory Application filed on behalf of appellant under Section 389 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for suspension of sentence/grant of bail during the pendency of the instant Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 329 of 2024 in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No.52 of 2021 (corresponding to CNR No.-JHCB01-002237-2021) arising out of Tonto P.S. Case No. 20 of 2021 against the judgment of conviction dated 13.12.2023 and order of sentence dated 14.12.2023 passed by learned Addl.
Sessions Judge-1-cum-Special Judge (POCSO) Act, West Singhbhum at Chaibasa, whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(3) of the IPC and under Section 4(2) of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 24 years for the offence punishable under Section 4(2) of the POCSO Act and directed to pay a fine of Rs. 20,000/- and in default of fine,
further directed to undergo additional S.I. for one year.
No sentence has been passed under Section 376(3) of IPC in view of the provisions of Section 42 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 2. The argument has been advanced on behalf of the appellant that it is a case where the prosecution has miserably failed in establishing the charges said to be proved beyond all reasonable doubt.
The submission has also been made that the Doctor has not supported the prosecution version and as such it is a fit case where the sentence is required to be suspended.
3. While on the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
It has been contended that P.W.-1, the victim has fully supported the prosecution version.
The submission has also been made that P.W.-6,
the brother has also supported the prosecution version

. So far as the argument that the Doctor has not found any sign of sexual assault, the same cannot be said to be fatal for the prosecution in view of the fact that PW-1, the victim has fully supported the prosecution version.
Learned counsel for the State based upon the aforesaid grounds therefore submitted that it is not a fit case where sentences is required to be suspended.

4. This Court has heard the learned counsel for the parties and gone across the findings recorded by learned trial Court in the impugned judgment passed as also the testimony of the witnesses and evidences as available in the Lower Court Record and other material exhibits.

5. This court after going through the testimony of P.W.-1, the victim and the P.W.-6, the brother of the victim who have fully supported the prosecution version, is of the view that the case is not in nature where the sentence is to be suspended.

Further so far as having found no sign of rape by the Doctor cannot be said to be vital for the prosecution and cannot be ground to say that the prosecution has failed in proving the charge, rather, P.W.-1, the victim and P.W.-6, the brother has fully supported the prosecution version.
6. Considering the aforesaid fact, this Court is of the view that it is not a case where the sentence is to be suspended.
7. In consequence thereof, the instant interlocutory application i.e. I.A. No. 5135 of 2024 stands rejected and as such disposed of.

8. It is made clear that any observation made hereinabove will not prejudice the case on merit, since,
the criminal appeal is pending before this Court for its consideration.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Navneet Kumar, J.) Basant/S.Das 2 Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No. 329 of 2024 Ramja Kondankel Aged About 35 Years S/O ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126481195/
